pin_variations.title: Meal Prep Magic: Sheet Pan Tomato Basil Soup Under 200 Calories
pin_variations.description: Looking for easy meal prep ideas? This tomato basil soup is a winner—high protein, low calorie, and full of flavor. Make a big batch and enjoy all week long. Pin for your next meal prep day! 🍅🥄 #mealprep #highprotein #lowcalorie #healthyrecipes

ingredients: 1 scoop unflavored whey protein isolate powder
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
yield: Approximately 1.5 cups of soup per serving, 6 servings total
introduction: I’ve always struggled with feeling hungry on low-calorie diets, especially when I’m trying to cut but hate tiny snack portions. This sheet pan tomato basil soup became my afternoon lifesaver because it’s big on volume but low on calories. Roasting the tomatoes and basil on a sheet pan really amps up the flavor without adding fat, which is a game changer. I add cottage cheese and a scoop of whey protein isolate to boost the protein without making the soup heavy or creamy with fat. The trick to keeping it light but satisfying is using low-fat dairy and protein powder, which helps keep me full for hours. Plus, the texture is silky smooth, and it’s so easy to make—just roast, blend, and stir. I’ve tried making it with different yogurts before, but zero-fat cottage cheese gives the best balance of creaminess and protein without wateriness. My friends always ask how I eat so much soup and still stay within my calorie goals—it’s all about volume and smart ingredients. This recipe is perfect for meal prep Sundays or a quick post-workout snack when you want something warm and nourishing but not heavy.

instructions.instruction: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Arrange the halved tomatoes, quartered onion, garlic cloves, and basil leaves on a large rimmed sheet pan. Drizzle with a teaspoon of olive oil if you want a bit of caramelization, but you can skip it for fewer calories. Roast for about 20 minutes until the tomatoes are softened and lightly charred. Roasting concentrates the flavors and reduces water content, so your soup won’t be watery. Avoid overcrowding the pan to ensure even roasting and prevent steaming instead of roasting.
instructions.doneness_cue: Tomatoes should be visibly softened with some charred edges, onions translucent and fragrant

instructions.instruction: Once roasted, transfer the vegetables and basil to a blender. Add the low-fat cottage cheese, unsweetened almond milk, and whey protein isolate powder. Blend on high until smooth and creamy. The protein powder hydrates and thickens the soup without adding fat, but blend thoroughly to avoid chalkiness. If the soup feels too thick, add a splash more almond milk. Avoid blending too long or the soup might get too frothy.
instructions.doneness_cue: Smooth, creamy texture with no visible lumps or powder residue

why_this_recipe_works.section: Why This High-Protein Low-Calorie Soup Fills You Up Without Guilt
why_this_recipe_works.content:
Protein has a higher thermic effect of food (TEF) compared to carbs and fats, meaning your body burns more calories digesting it. This soup packs whey protein isolate and cottage cheese, both excellent sources that trigger satiety hormones like PYY and GLP-1, helping you feel full longer. Combining these with low-calorie, high-volume roasted tomatoes and basil stretches your stomach, sending mechanical fullness signals to your brain.

Roasting the tomatoes reduces their water content and intensifies flavor without adding calories, so you get a rich taste without fat. Using zero-fat cottage cheese and whey isolate avoids the calorie density of nuts or oils but maintains creaminess. The protein powder thickens the soup, and blending with almond milk prevents chalkiness by hydrating the powder properly.

Hydrocolloids like xanthan gum aren’t needed here because the roasting and protein powder create a natural creamy texture. Large portion sizes satisfy cravings psychologically, so you feel like you’re eating a hearty meal, not a skimpy snack. This balance of volume, protein, and flavor makes this soup perfect for anyone cutting calories but wanting to enjoy their food.

ingredient_notes.whey protein isolate powder: Choose a high-quality unflavored whey protein isolate with minimal additives and no maltodextrin to keep calories low and avoid aftertaste. Whey isolate is ideal because it has very little fat and carbs, making it perfect for low-calorie snacks. It hydrates quickly in liquids, thickening the soup without chalkiness if blended well.
ingredient_notes.low-fat cottage cheese: Opt for 1% or 2% cottage cheese with minimal sodium and no added cream. Zero-fat versions can sometimes be watery, so choose a brand with good texture. Cottage cheese adds creaminess and protein without fat, helping the soup feel rich without extra calories. Avoid full-fat varieties to maintain low calorie count.
ingredient_notes.fresh tomatoes: Use ripe, firm tomatoes for the best flavor and sweetness. Roasting them concentrates natural sugars and reduces water content, ensuring a thick soup without needing cream or oils. Avoid canned tomatoes with added salt or preservatives for a cleaner taste.
ingredient_notes.fresh basil leaves: Fresh basil adds bright herbal notes that balance the acidity of tomatoes. It also contributes antioxidants without calories. Adding basil during roasting releases essential oils that enhance flavor depth.
ingredient_notes.unsweetened almond milk: Use unsweetened almond milk as a low-calorie liquid base. It hydrates the protein powder and smooths the texture without adding sugar or fat. Avoid flavored or sweetened versions to keep calories minimal.

pro_tips.tip: Don’t skip roasting the tomatoes and basil before blending.
pro_tips.reason: Roasting reduces water content and intensifies flavors, preventing a watery, bland soup. It also caramelizes natural sugars, adding depth without calories. Skipping this step results in a thin, less flavorful soup.

pro_tips.tip: Blend the protein powder thoroughly with almond milk before adding cottage cheese.
pro_tips.reason: Proper hydration prevents chalkiness and lumps. Mixing protein powder directly with dairy can cause clumps. Pre-mixing ensures a smooth, creamy texture that blends seamlessly into the soup.

pro_tips.tip: Use fresh, ripe tomatoes for best results.
pro_tips.reason: They have higher natural sugar content, which caramelizes when roasted, producing a sweeter, richer soup. Overripe or mealy tomatoes can make the soup watery or bland.

common_mistakes_to_avoid.mistake: Skipping roasting and blending raw tomatoes directly.
common_mistakes_to_avoid.why_it_happens: People often want to save time and blend raw ingredients, assuming it’s faster and just as tasty.
common_mistakes_to_avoid.fix: Always roast the tomatoes and basil first. This step is crucial for flavor concentration and reducing excess water, which keeps the soup thick and rich without added fat.

common_mistakes_to_avoid.mistake: Using full-fat dairy or too much oil.
common_mistakes_to_avoid.why_it_happens: Many assume creaminess requires fat, so they add heavy cream or extra oil.
common_mistakes_to_avoid.fix: Stick to low-fat cottage cheese and minimal oil. The protein powder and roasting technique provide creaminess without extra calories or fat.

common_mistakes_to_avoid.mistake: Adding protein powder last without proper mixing.
common_mistakes_to_avoid.why_it_happens: Rushing the process leads to clumps or chalky texture.
common_mistakes_to_avoid.fix: Blend protein powder with almond milk first to hydrate it well, then add to the soup base for a smooth finish.

storage_and_reheating.room_temperature: This soup should not be left out at room temperature for more than 2 hours due to dairy content. Cover with a lid or plastic wrap if you need to hold it briefly.
storage_and_reheating.refrigerator: Store in an airtight container for up to 4 days. The soup thickens when chilled but can be thinned with a splash of almond milk when reheated. Flavor often improves after a day as ingredients meld.
storage_and_reheating.freezer: Freeze in portioned containers for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently on the stove or microwave. Texture may become slightly grainy due to cottage cheese but still tastes great.
storage_and_reheating.reheating: Reheat on low-medium heat stirring occasionally to prevent separation. Avoid boiling to keep texture smooth. Add a little almond milk if soup is too thick.
storage_and_reheating.make_ahead_strategy: Roast the vegetables and basil up to 2 days in advance and store roasted veggies refrigerated. Blend with dairy and protein powder fresh before serving to maintain best texture and flavor.

faq.question: Can I substitute the whey protein isolate with another protein powder?
faq.answer: Yes, but choose a protein powder that hydrates well and has a neutral flavor to avoid chalkiness or off-tastes. Pea or soy protein powders can work but may affect texture and flavor slightly. Always blend powder with liquid first for best results.

faq.question: What if I don’t have cottage cheese? Can I use Greek yogurt?
faq.answer: You can substitute with 0% Greek yogurt, but it may make the soup tangier and thinner. Greek yogurt also has a different texture, so blend carefully to avoid separation. Cottage cheese gives a creamier texture with slightly less tang.

faq.question: Is this soup suitable for meal prep?
faq.answer: Absolutely! It stores well in the fridge for up to 4 days and can be frozen. Just reheat gently and add a splash of almond milk if it thickens too much. It’s a great make-ahead snack or light meal.

faq.question: How can I avoid the soup tasting chalky from protein powder?
faq.answer: The key is to blend the protein powder with almond milk first to hydrate it fully before adding to the soup. Also, using unflavored whey isolate with no fillers helps prevent chalkiness. Avoid adding powder directly to hot soup.

faq.question: Can I add more vegetables to increase volume?
faq.answer: Yes, adding low-calorie veggies like spinach or roasted red peppers works well. Just adjust seasoning and liquid slightly to maintain texture and flavor balance.

faq.question: When is the best time to eat this soup for maximum benefit?
faq.answer: It’s great as a post-workout snack or during an afternoon slump because it provides protein to aid recovery and keeps you full with low calories. Also ideal for meal prep days when you want a quick, nutritious snack.

faq.question: How do I keep the soup from being watery?
faq.answer: Roasting the tomatoes properly reduces water content. Avoid adding too much almond milk initially and blend until smooth. If too watery, simmer gently to reduce or add more protein powder for thickness.

faq.question: Can I make this soup spicy?
faq.answer: Definitely! Add a pinch of cayenne pepper or red chili flakes to the roasting pan or blend them in with the soup. It pairs nicely with the sweetness of roasted tomatoes and basil.

conclusion: Give this sheet pan tomato basil soup a try and enjoy a satisfying, protein-rich snack that keeps calories in check. Share your results or tag me if you make it—I’d love to see how you enjoy it!
